method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, reverse reconstruction of the saturated and complete extension argument, both identity branches, the semantic-to-syntactic contraposition proof, and the paired FOL/propositional exercises, followed by exact formula, macro, controlled-token, tag, label, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: The Completeness Theorem in satisfiability and entailment-to-derivability forms, including first-order identity and propositional tagged branches.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Every consistent sentence set is satisfiable. In FOL, first take a saturated consistent extension and then a complete consistent extension, which remains saturated; the Truth Lemma supplies a model when equality is absent and the quotient-model Truth Lemma handles equality. The propositional branch lets its complete consistent extension determine a satisfying valuation.
samples.checks: Gamma, Gamma-prime and Gamma-star inclusions, both Henkin conditionals, identity split, model or valuation satisfaction, sentence membership and satisfiability conclusion are all exact.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: The second version says semantic entailment implies derivability. Restating the first theorem with Delta and contraposing shows that any unsatisfiable sentence set is inconsistent; entailment makes Gamma union not-A unsatisfiable, and the cited inconsistency result yields Gamma proves A.
samples.checks: Universal scope, every Delta occurrence, contraposition direction, union with not-A, semantic reference, four proof-system reference branches and final derivability claim are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Paired tagged exercises ask for the reverse derivation of the first completeness formulation from the second, establishing equivalence for FOL and propositional logic.
samples.checks: Each language guard and fully qualified theorem and corollary reference is unchanged.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Paired exercises ask which derivation rules make every unsatisfiable set provably inconsistent and request a dependency list or diagram, including tacit rule uses, for the completeness proof.
samples.checks: Completeness, unsatisfiability, inconsistency, rule-use dependencies, tacit uses and both language-specific theorem references remain exact.

source_observations: The first theorem covers equality-free FOL with the term-model Truth Lemma and equality-containing FOL with the quotient-model Truth Lemma; both branches are explicit in the target.
The same source file also produces a propositional build through FOL and notFOL tags; every guard and branch is preserved.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, tags, labels, identifiers and reference options match exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
अनुप्रमेय is directly supported as a general theorem role by MR-P104, but its use throughout formal logic remains expert-reviewable under T198.
The rule-dependency diagrams and reverse completeness proofs requested as exercises are not supplied.
